newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Vanik says to buy two firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Vanik says to buy two firms.

text.p: Sri Lankan investment bank Vanik Incorporation Ltd said in a statement on Wednesday that it proposed buying two companies to maintain its competitive edge in the market.

The statement said Vanik had informed shareholders of its decision to buy Forbes & Walker, a Colombo-based commodity and stock broking firm, and Forbes & Walker International, a Bermuda registered holding company which controls Forbes Ceylon Ltd.

"Though we have an understanding with regard to the purchase price, it cannot be revealed yet since no definitive agreement has been signed," Justin Meegoda, president and chief executive of Vanik told Reuters.
"As long as it meets with the approval of all the authorities concerned, we don't have anything against it," said Ajit Jayaratne, chairman of Forbes & Walker.
The total assets of the two companies are valued at 2.59 billion rupees, the statement said.
It added the company was calling an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of its shareholders on March 5 to seek approval for the purcahse of the two firms.

An EGM is necessary since Asia Capital Ltd, which made an offer to buy Vanik, has launched court action to prevent Vanik from acquiring the two firms without shareholder approval, the statement added.
Investment bank Asia Capital said in January that it planned to buy Vanik's entire issued capital for eight rupees in cash and one new share of its own.
The Asia Capital offer is pending because the company has yet to seek the Securities and Exchange Commission's approval.
